reviews.one_line_contribution: A zero-rollout statistic — mean pairwise Jaccard overlap of top-k retrieval sets — is offered as a pre-deployment predictor of whether per-instance retrieval over a procedural memory bank can be replaced, verbatim and token-matched, by a fixed subset of that same bank, plus a redundancy (rather than interference) reinterpretation of ReasoningBank's 49.7%@k=1 → 44.4%@k=4 ablation that is decided by an MMR-diversified retrieval cell.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, and the proposal only engages one. (1) arXiv:2511.21730 (Nov 2025), which the author concedes: it establishes on ALFWorld that embedding retrievers over procedural items behave as unordered bags of words and fail to discriminate context — i.e. it already supplies the mediator this proposal proposes to measure, and 2602.02751 plus 2606.23127 already supply the end-to-end direction (saturation, retrieval collapsing the gain). What survives is the overlap law itself, and the law is the part most compromised by the definitional objection below. (2) The threat the Collision Check never looked for at all: the in-context-learning demonstration-selection literature, where per-instance kNN/similarity retrieval of demonstrations versus a single fixed demonstration set has been compared repeatedly and frequently ties, with the tie explained by exactly the mechanism proposed here (near-identical retrieved sets across queries). The frozen-subset swap is that experiment with 'demonstrations' renamed 'procedural memory items'. The proposal distinguishes itself from factual RAG-vs-long-context (Related Work §7) but never from retrieval-vs-fixed demonstration selection, which is far closer to its actual design: same k, same items, verbatim, token-matched, no compiler. A reviewer who knows that line will read A_fix as a known-null ablation transplanted to a new bank type.
reviews.strongest_objection: Falsifiable Prediction 1 and the high-overlap half of Prediction 2 are near-tautological, and the design pins both ends of the regression by construction. A_fix is the k highest-dev-frequency items; O is the mean pairwise Jaccard of the top-k sets those items are drawn from. At O = 1.0, A_ret and A_fix are literally the same k items for every instance, so R_fix = 0 by identity, not by measurement — the E2-narrow cell (claimed O > 0.7) and the highest-overlap E1 cells are therefore testing arithmetic plus decoding noise. At O = 0.5 with k=7, roughly half of each query's retrieved items are already in any other query's set, and the frequency-selected fixed subset captures most of the rest, so 'R_fix < 2 points' is what the statistic mechanically implies, not a risky prediction about whether query conditioning carries information. At the other end, both low-overlap anchors are engineered to make R_fix large: B-dup seeds paraphrase near-duplicates of specific test instances (instance-specific by construction, as the proposal says), and E-mix unions two procedurally disjoint families so that a single fixed block must serve both. The leave-one-cell-out test in Prediction 2 then fits a curve whose endpoints are fixed analytically and by design, over ~20 cells that are not independent (shared agent, scaffold, training split, and in most cases the same B_expel bank), with k* — one of the four overlap knobs — chosen per cell to maximize A_ret accuracy, which entangles the predictor with the outcome it is supposed to predict out of sample. The acc(A_ret)−acc(A0) covariate guards against inert-memory cells but does nothing about this. Second, a checkable internal inconsistency: Prediction 1 requires per-cell TOST at a 4-point margin to pass in ≥8 of ~11 high-overlap cells, but Measurement §(b) states that at n=600 equivalence at margin 4 requires an observed gap ≤1.4, and §MDE gives n=300 → MDE ≈6, E2-broad n=140 → MDE ≈8, E2-narrow n=100 → MDE ≈9. Counting the A_fix cells actually planned, only about four run at n=600 (B_expel N=500, N=1000, the k=7 volume cell, B_rbank); the rest are n=300 subsamples (B-dup, A_rand, both cross-model families) or n=100–140 ALFWorld cells where TOST at a 4-point margin cannot pass even with a true zero difference. Prediction 1 as written is close to unachievable arithmetically, and Prediction 4's numeric claims for E2-narrow (R_fix < 2) and the ≥3-point narrow-vs-broad contrast are stated at a resolution below that cell's own declared MDE of 8–9.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (a) Decontaminate the law. Report R_fix against an explicit analytic null: given the measured top-k sets and the frequency-selected fixed subset, compute the expected R_fix under a model in which the agent uses only the items common to both arms, and show that observed R_fix departs from that curve. Equivalently, restrict the headline regression to cells in a mid range (say O ∈ [0.2, 0.8]) at a single fixed k, and report the O ≈ 1 and B-dup cells as sanity endpoints rather than as data points that carry the fit. Without this, the paper's central number is a property of the definition of O, not of procedural memory. (b) Decouple k* selection from O by fixing k across the cells that enter the regression, and report the k*-selected version as a secondary. (c) Reconcile Prediction 1 with the MDE table: either drop per-cell TOST and make the inverse-variance random-effects meta-estimate the only equivalence claim (as Measurement §(b) already implies), or raise the margin and state honestly how many cells are powered. (d) Restate the E2 predictions as directional, since the design cannot resolve a 2-point R_fix at n=100. (e) Add the upper-bound retrieval arm named below, so a null on R_fix can be attributed to query conditioning rather than to a weak dense retriever — this is the single change that would most raise soundness, and it is cheap relative to the arms already budgeted.
reviews.missing_baseline: An upper-bound retrieval arm. The plan has A_rand as a lower bound but nothing above A_ret, so 'the retriever is decorative' cannot be separated from 'this dense/BM25 retriever extracts none of the available query-conditional signal' — which is precisely what the proposal's own mechanistic ally (2511.21730: embeddings treat procedures as bags of words, discarding temporal structure; LLM-generated abstractions transfer reliably) predicts is happening. Concretely: an oracle-relevance arm (select the k bank items whose source training instances are the gold-matched or human/LLM-labelled relevant ones for each test instance) and/or an LLM-reranker arm over the whole bank at the same k and matched tokens. If oracle retrieval also ties with A_fix, the claim is strong and general; if it beats A_fix by ≥4 points where dense retrieval does not, the paper's title is answered 'the retriever is bad, not decorative' and the deliverable diagnostic is measuring retriever weakness rather than a property of procedural memory. Secondary omission: a whole-bank-in-context arm without compilation at N=100 (the raw RAG-vs-long-context comparison the proposal invokes in Related Work §7 but never runs; A_comp is a frontier-model compilation, not stuffing).
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually good by the standards of this genre — it quotes rather than paraphrases, explicitly withdraws five IDs an earlier draft relied on, reinstates Memp only because it reappeared in the current search, concedes that 2602.02751 outright scoops the bank-size saturation claim, and concedes 2511.21730 as a direction-level collision. I judge it honest and I do not find a preprint that already makes the specific overlap-predicts-premium claim. Three residual weaknesses, though, and they matter. First, the check is grounded entirely in one literature search's returns, with no OpenReview 2026 sweep and no independent verification pass; the author flags this as residual risk, which is the right disclosure but does not remove the exposure, given that a frozen-retrieved-subset ablation is exactly the kind of thing that lives in an appendix. Second, and more seriously, the check never searched the nearest neighbouring literature at all: retrieval-based versus fixed in-context demonstration selection, where the same swap has been run for years with frequently null results. The RAG-vs-long-context parallel is raised and answered, but the demonstration-selection parallel — which is the actual shape of A_fix — is absent from the search and from Related Work. An unsearched adjacent literature is a hole in the novelty argument, not a neutral. Third, the concessions the check does make add up to more than it concludes: with the direction attributed to 2511.21730/2602.02751/2606.23127 and the write-path abstraction to AWM/Auto-Dreamer, the entire remaining novelty rests on the overlap law and the MMR sign test — and the law is the component compromised by the definitional objection above, leaving the MMR discriminating test against 2606.29824 as the cleanest genuinely new thing in the proposal.

reviews.one_line_contribution: Per-instance retrieval in procedural agent memory (ExpeL/ReasoningBank/Memp-style) can be replaced end-to-end by a fixed, verbatim, top-frequency subset of the same bank at no accuracy cost whenever the retriever's top-k sets are already near-identical across queries, and a rollout-free mean-pairwise-Jaccard statistic predicts out of sample both when that holds and whether injecting more items helps or hurts.
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv:2511.21730 (procedural memory retrieval benchmark) combined with arXiv:2602.02751 (strategy auctions). The proposal concedes both, correctly. 2511.21730 already establishes the mediator the paper depends on — that embedding retrievers on procedural items behave as unordered bags of words and cannot separate functionally distinct procedures — and 2602.02751 already establishes that the only real transition is M=0 to M>0. Between them, a reader has the mechanism and the saturation; what remains for this proposal is the end-to-end swap and the quantitative mapping. That is a real gap (neither re-runs the agent with the retriever frozen, neither token-matches), but it is an ablation-shaped gap, not a new phenomenon. The second threat is the long-context-vs-RAG literature, which the proposal engages only in prose (Related Work §7): the claim that retrieval's value is regime-dependent along a query-differentiation axis is not new there, and the proposal runs no factual-RAG cell, so its own stated falsifier ('if procedural and factual-RAG cells did not sit at opposite ends of the overlap axis, the law would be falsified') is asserted and never tested.
reviews.strongest_objection: The central law is close to analytic at the end where it will be confirmed. O = mean pairwise Jaccard of top-k sets is, by construction, a measure of how much A_ret's per-instance injected content differs from any fixed k-item block; as O -> 1, A_ret and A_fix are literally the same prompt on most instances, so R_fix ~ 0 is guaranteed by the manipulation check rather than discovered. 'Overlap predicts the retrieval premium' then reduces to 'the size of the outcome difference tracks the size of the treatment difference.' The non-trivial half of the law is the O < 0.25 end (Prediction 2: 'every cell with O < 0.25 has R_fix >= 8'), and there the design is anchored almost entirely on manufactured cells: B-dup is paraphrase near-duplicates seeded against specific test instances, and E-mix is a two-environment splice. After excluding B-dup as the proposal itself requires, the low-overlap end of a ~20-point regression rests on essentially E-mix (tested twice) — so the Spearman rho <= -0.6 requirement on non-synthetic cells is decided by one or two points. Compounding this, O is not independent of the knobs used to move it: mean pairwise Jaccard is mechanically a function of k and N, and k and N are two of the four 'independent' knobs, which also confounds Prediction 6 (V is compared across k=1 and k=7 cells whose O values differ partly because k differs). Second, load-bearing predictions are stated at thresholds their own MDEs cannot resolve. Prediction 4 — which the proposal itself calls 'the prediction that decides whether our claim is about procedural memory or only about template-repeating benchmarks' — is a difference-in-differences between E2-narrow (n=100, stated MDE ~9) and E2-broad (n=140, stated MDE ~8), so the SE on that >=3-point contrast is roughly 6 points; it is powered at a small fraction of what it claims, and 'R_fix < 2' cannot be established by TOST at margin 4 at n=100 by the proposal's own arithmetic (equivalence needs an observed gap <= 1.4 at n=600). Third, the cell accounting does not reconstruct: Prediction 1 asserts TOST passing in '>=8 of the ~11' O>0.5 cells, but the E1 table runs A_fix in only about six cells (B_expel N=500 and N=1000, the k=7 volume cell, B_rbank, E-mix-on-E1, B-dup) plus three on E2 and four cross-model — and the proposal states it will 'report per model and never pool,' which strands the cross-model cells. Fourth, gate G1 (every bank must beat A0 by >=8 points) is a precondition the memory literature and this track's own prior results suggest frequently fails; if it fails broadly, most cells become 'memory inert here' and the regression has no cells left, which is a plausible modal outcome rather than a tail risk. Finally, the headline that the diagnostic is 'computable in seconds, zero agent rollouts' is inconsistent with the fitted model, which conditions on acc(A_ret) - acc(A0) as a covariate and gates cells on G1 — both of which require rollouts. The LOO test uses O alone while the reported fit is covariate-adjusted; these are different models and the paper should not be allowed to advertise one and estimate the other.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: The cheapest and most decisive fix costs zero extra episodes: report R_fix restricted to the subset of instances on which the retrieved set actually differs from the frozen set. If per-instance conditioning is worthless even on the instances where it changes the prompt, the claim is empirical rather than definitional, and the paper survives the tautology objection that will otherwise sink it. Report that conditional R_fix alongside the marginal one in every high-overlap cell, and regress on it. Second, add a retrieval ceiling: an oracle or LLM-reranker read path (2511.21730's own finding is that LLM-generated abstractions transfer where embeddings do not), so a null can be attributed to query-conditioning rather than to weak dense/BM25/MMR retrievers. Third, re-power the E2 narrow-vs-broad contrast — it is the only within-environment, non-manufactured diversity manipulation in the design and is currently the weakest cell in the study; take episodes from the B_expel N in {250} bank sweep and the A_rand draws to bring both E2 cells toward n=400+, or demote Prediction 4 to descriptive and stop calling it decisive. Fourth, add at least one non-synthetic low-overlap cell that is not an environment splice (e.g., a genuinely heterogeneous single-environment suite, or WebArena/tool-agent tasks with distinct sub-goals) so the fitted crossing threshold is not carried by B-dup and E-mix. Fifth, decouple O from k: either report O at a fixed k for all cells, or fit R_fix on O with k and N as explicit covariates, so the law is not partly recovering an arithmetic identity. Sixth, either run one factual-RAG cell to test the low-overlap-limit claim, or delete that falsification condition from the paper.
reviews.missing_baseline: A retrieval upper bound. There is no oracle-retrieval or LLM-reranker arm establishing that per-instance conditioning has any headroom in this setup, so R_fix ~ 0 is ambiguous between 'the read path is decorative' and 'dense/BM25/MMR retrievers over strategy-level items are bag-of-words weak' — and 2511.21730, which the proposal cites approvingly, already reported the latter. Without a ceiling, the paper's title claim is unearned and a reviewer will demand the cell. Secondary omissions: (a) a best-fixed-subset arm chosen on dev to maximize accuracy rather than retrieval frequency — A_fix as specified (highest dev retrieval frequency) is not the strongest static competitor, which makes A_fix an odd primary arm to hang an equivalence claim on; and (b) a raw whole-bank-in-context arm at N=100, the direct long-context control the RAG parallel in Related Work §7 invites and that A_comp (frontier-compiled) does not substitute for.
reviews.preprint_collision: Among the more serious collision checks I have seen: it quotes specific text, names 2511.21730 as a real partial collision and concedes it, concedes outright that 2602.02751 scoops the bank-size saturation claim and demotes that claim accordingly, and explicitly withdraws five arXiv IDs relied on in a prior draft. That is the right behavior and I credit it. Three reservations keep it from being a clean pass. (1) The check itself discloses that an earlier draft of this same line of work cited arXiv IDs the author could not find in search results; that history should discount, not increase, a reviewer's confidence in the quoted passages here, several of which (2602.02751, 2605.20616, 2606.23127, 2606.29824, 2607.01480) I cannot verify and which are dated within the last several months. The proposal's own rule — nothing enters the novelty argument unless it appears in a quotable search result — is the right rule, but it does not make the quotes checkable by me. (2) No OpenReview or venue-submission sweep, which the proposal admits; a 'freeze the retrieved subset' ablation in the appendix of a combined-system submission is exactly the kind of thing that sweep would find, and it would remove the paper's primary arm. (3) The RAG-vs-long-context literature is engaged only in prose with no paper named, despite the proposal staking an explicit falsification condition on where factual-RAG cells sit on its overlap axis. Net: no preprint I can name already makes the full claim, but the check's own concessions leave the residual novelty thin — the direction is conceded as converging across 2511.21730, 2602.02751 and 2606.23127, so the paper stands or falls on the predictive law, which is the part most vulnerable to the tautology objection above.

reviews.one_line_contribution: Replace per-instance top-k retrieval in procedural agent memory with the k most-frequently-retrieved items held fixed and verbatim for every query (the A_fix arm), and claim that mean pairwise top-k Jaccard overlap O, computable from the retriever with zero rollouts, predicts out of sample how much end-to-end accuracy that swap costs.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal correctly names arXiv:2511.21730 as a partial collision on direction, but the work that most threatens novelty is one it never engages: the in-context demonstration-selection literature, where 'retrieved demonstrations vs a fixed/random demonstration set costs little' is a long-standing and repeatedly replicated finding on exactly the demonstration slot this track is framed around. Related Work item (7) pre-empts only the RAG-vs-long-context parallel and treats the objection as being about corpora; the demo-selection line is about k retrieved exemplars in a prompt, which is structurally identical to A_ret vs A_fix, and its known answer (fixed exemplars are usually within noise of retrieved ones on homogeneous task distributions) is the proposal's Prediction 1. Also unengaged: adaptive-retrieval / retrieval-necessity work in RAG, which already builds predictors of whether retrieval will pay, weakening the 'first pre-deployment diagnostic' framing to 'first corpus-level diagnostic for procedural banks'. Combined with the author's own concession that 2602.02751 scoops bank-size saturation outright and 2511.21730 establishes the direction, what is left as new is one statistic and one MMR cell.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline law is close to an analytic identity, and the proposal never states the null that would show otherwise. O is defined as the mean pairwise Jaccard of the top-k sets, and A_fix injects (approximately) the modal top-k set; so O is a direct measure of how much of A_ret's prompt A_fix already reproduces. At O near 1.0 the two arms literally inject the same k items for nearly every test instance, so R_fix must be ~0 by construction, not by discovery; at O near 0 they share almost nothing. Prediction 2's 'leave-one-cell-out prediction of R_fix from O beats a grand mean' is therefore largely the statement that two conditions differ more in accuracy when they differ more in content, and the fitted 'crossing threshold' shipped as the deliverable inherits that. The proposal offers no analytic baseline (e.g. expected R_fix under a pure content-difference model scaling with (1-O) times the measured marginal per-item effect) against which the fit could be shown to carry information beyond the identity. Two reinforcing problems: (a) O is collinear with the very knobs used to move it - Jaccard falls mechanically as N grows and its scale is not comparable across k in {1,3,7} (at k=1 pairwise Jaccard is binary and reduces to modal-item frequency), so a 20-cell regression that pools cells differing simultaneously in environment, bank, N, retriever and k cannot separate O from 'which cell this is', and only two contrasts (dense vs MMR, E2-narrow vs E2-broad) vary diversity at fixed everything else; (b) with no retrieval upper bound in the design, a null R_fix cannot distinguish 'no per-instance information exists in this bank' from 'dense embedding retrieval over strategy-level items cannot find it' - which is precisely what the proposal's own cited ally 2511.21730 already demonstrated ('embeddings fundamentally treat procedures as unordered bags of words'). Under that reading the correct conclusion is 'fix the retriever', not 'the retriever is decorative', and the paper's title claim collapses. Secondary but concrete: Predictions 1 and 6 sit in tension - if MMR recovers >=3 points over dense at the same bank and k=7 in an O>0.5 cell while A_fix ties dense within 2 points, then a per-instance retrieval variant beats the frozen arm, which is the opposite of decorative, and no diversified-frozen-subset arm exists to resolve it. And the power arithmetic does not support Prediction 1: TOST needs more power than NHST, the stated single-cell MDEs are 4 (n=600), 6 (n=300) and 8-9 (E2 n=140/100), and by my count only about six of the roughly eleven high-overlap R_fix cells run at n=600, so 'per-cell TOST equivalence at a 4-point margin passes in >=8 of ~11 cells' is close to arithmetically unreachable as designed.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Publish the analytic null for the law: predict R_fix from (1-O) times the measured marginal effect of swapping one injected item, and require the O-fit to beat that, not just a grand mean - otherwise the diagnostic is a restatement of prompt distance. 2) Add at least three cells where O is moved with environment, bank, N and k all held fixed (retrieval temperature, embedding model, MMR lambda sweep); a law identified only across heterogeneous cells is not identified. 3) Normalize O against its random-set expectation so cells at k=1, 3 and 7 are on a comparable axis, and pre-register that normalized statistic rather than raw Jaccard. 4) Add a retrieval ceiling (oracle or task-type-labelled selection) so a null separates 'no instance-specific signal' from 'weak retriever'. 5) Add A_fix-MMR (diversity-selected frozen subset) so Prediction 6's MMR gain can be attributed to redundancy removal rather than to per-instance conditioning; without it Predictions 1 and 6 cannot both be reported as supporting the thesis. 6) Restate Prediction 1 as the random-effects meta-estimate only, and drop or re-power the per-cell TOST count, which the stated MDEs cannot deliver. 7) Either reproduce ReasoningBank's setup or demote claim (iii) from 'reinterprets their k-curve' to 'makes a compatible prediction in our setup' - the current wording promises a reinterpretation of numbers obtained on a different scaffold, models and benchmark.
reviews.missing_baseline: A mismatched-retrieval arm: per-instance top-k retrieval driven by a different, randomly paired test query's embedding. This is the arm that separates the two things A_fix confounds - loss of query conditioning versus loss of any per-instance variation in the injected block - and it is the first thing a reviewer will demand of a paper whose thesis is 'query conditioning does nothing'. The listed 'shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check' is described as a check that the retriever functions, not as this control, and A_rand is a fixed subset (no per-instance variation), so neither substitutes. Also absent: a retrieval upper bound (oracle item selection) to rule out 'weak retriever' as the explanation of a null, a diversified frozen subset (A_fix-MMR), and the plain long-context arm - the whole bank stuffed verbatim at N=100 - which is the natural RAG-vs-long-context comparator the proposal invokes in Related Work item (7) but never runs, since A_comp is a frontier-compiled summary instead.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above the median for this kind of check, and I credit it: it quotes text rather than gesturing, explicitly withdraws five arXiv IDs an earlier draft leaned on, reinstates one that the current search did return, concedes that 2602.02751 scoops the bank-size saturation claim outright, and concedes 2511.21730 as a partial collision on direction. It also adopts the search's own verdict that the direction is converging across 2025-2026 work - which is a real finding against the proposal's novelty, and the honest concession does not undo the deduction. Two substantive weaknesses. First, the author's standing rule ('nothing enters the novelty argument unless it appears in a search result I can quote') makes the check self-limiting: entire adjacent literatures that were not returned - in-context demonstration selection, adaptive/necessity-of-retrieval prediction, retrieval-vs-long-context - are excluded by construction, and only the last gets a paragraph in Related Work rather than a collision entry. That is exactly where I would expect the fatal precedent for 'fixed exemplars tie retrieved exemplars' to sit. Second, the disclosed history of fabricated IDs in a prior draft leaves residual verification risk on the load-bearing 2026 citations I cannot check here (2606.29824, 2602.02751, 2606.23127, 2607.01480, 2605.20616); if 2606.29824's pool-interference result exists as quoted, the mechanistic novelty reduces to a single MMR cell, and if it does not, the paper's designated rival account is unsourced. The admitted gap (no OpenReview 2026 sweep, and a 'freeze the retrieved subset' ablation plausibly living in some combined-system appendix) is the right residual risk to flag. Net: no outright collision named, but the check itself establishes that only the diagnostic and the volume-sign reinterpretation are novel, and both are the parts I judge weakest above.
